title: Pitch Deck Mastery: Persuasive Storytelling for Startup Fundraising

body_text: Crafting a Pitch Deck That Connects Design: Less Is More The design of your pitch deck is crucial. It's not just about the information you convey, but also about how you present it. A well-designed, visually harmonious deck reflects professionalism and attention to detail. Stick to a uniform color palette, use high-quality and relevant images, and keep your text minimal. Each slide should communicate a single central idea, avoiding clutter and enhancing the investor's understanding​​. Speak with Numbers Numbers and data are powerful tools in a pitch deck. They provide tangible evidence of your startup's progress and potential. Use the latest statistics and market research to build credibility. However, avoid cluttering your slides with too much text or complex data. Simple, clear numbers that tell your story effectively are more impactful​​. Highlighting Market Opportunity Your pitch deck should not just focus on the product, but also on the market opportunity it addresses. Investors are interested in seeing the potential for profit. Research thoroughly to understand the market size, growth, and the specific audience you target. The entire deck should echo the potential of the market opportunity, including through traction​​. Realistic Business Plan and Financial Projections A clear, believable business plan and financial outlook are essential for your pitch deck. Utilize easy-to-understand charts and highlight your revenue streams, pricing strategy, customer data, and growth projections. Ensure your projections are grounded in reality and backed by research or industry models​​. Persuasive Call-to-Action End your pitch deck with a strong CTA. This creates urgency and can be the determining factor in securing the investment you seek. Whether it's a call for funding, partnership, or further discussions, make your ask clear and compelling. It's crucial that investors see a clear path forward and feel motivated to act​​. Empathy and Audience Understanding To make your pitch deck resonate, it needs to connect on an emotional level with your audience. Integrating empathy into your presentation builds trust and establishes an emotional bond with the investors. This connection is vital and goes beyond mere facts and figures, making your startup's story and vision more relatable and compelling​​. Impactful Headlines and Clean Design Your pitch deck's effectiveness also hinges on its headlines and overall design. Specific, vivid headlines help communicate the core message of each slide. The design should be clean, professional, and consistent, contributing to the overall narrative and making the deck memorable​​​​. Remember, in the competitive startup ecosystem, your pitch deck is a crucial tool for securing venture capital. It must stand out not just through its content, but also through its storytelling, design, and presentation. title: Soft Prompt Tuning for Augmenting Dense Retrieval with Large Language Models
summary: Tutorials, guides and deep dives into the best techniques and research for building reliable AI.
body_text: Do not index Original Paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08303 Blog URL Original Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08303 By: Zhiyuan Peng , Xuyang Wu , Qifan Wang , Yi Fang Abstract: Dense retrieval (DR) converts queries and documents into dense embeddings and measures the similarity between queries and documents in vector space. One of the challenges in DR is the lack of domain-specific training data. While DR models can learn from large-scale public datasets like MS MARCO through transfer learning, evidence shows that not all DR models and domains can benefit from transfer learning equally. Recently, some researchers have resorted to large language models (LLMs) to improve the zero-shot and few-shot DR models. However, the hard prompts or human-written prompts utilized in these works cannot guarantee the good quality of generated weak queries. To tackle this, we propose soft prompt tuning for augmenting DR (SPTAR): For each task, we leverage soft prompt-tuning to optimize a task-specific soft prompt on limited ground truth data and then prompt the LLMs to tag unlabeled documents with weak queries, yielding enough weak document-query pairs to train task-specific dense retrievers. We design a filter to select high-quality example document-query pairs in the prompt to further improve the quality of weak tagged queries. To the best of our knowledge, there is no prior work utilizing soft prompt tuning to augment DR models. The experiments demonstrate that SPTAR outperforms the unsupervised baselines BM25 and the recently proposed LLMs-based augmentation method for DR. Summary Notes Enhancing Dense Retrieval with Soft Prompt Tuning: A Revolution for AI Engineers The shift from traditional information retrieval (IR) methods to Dense Retrieval (DR) signifies a major advancement, especially for AI engineers in large companies. DR's success hinges on having access to ample, domain-specific training data, a hurdle that's hard to overcome. This blog introduces Soft Prompt Tuning for Augmenting Dense Retrieval (SPTAR) , a groundbreaking approach that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to create quality training data, tackling the data scarcity issue head-on. Understanding Dense Retrieval Before DR, IR systems relied on token-level similarity metrics like TF-IDF and BM25, which often missed the subtleties of language. DR improved upon this by using dense vector encodings for queries and documents, capturing semantic meanings more effectively. Yet, DR's efficiency is limited by the availability of specialized training data. Introducing SPTAR The rise of LLMs, such as GPT-3, has opened new doors for learning with minimal examples. SPTAR capitalizes on this, using soft prompt tuning to craft weak queries for documents without labels. This innovative method not only solves the data shortage problem but also upgrades the training data quality for DR models. What is Soft Prompt Tuning? Soft Prompt Tuning is a game-changer because it uses adaptable vectors (soft prompts) rather than fixed ones. This adaptability means the model can fine-tune its responses for specific tasks, leading to more accurate outcomes. The key steps are: Optimizing a task-specific soft prompt with a small amount of accurate data. Creating weak queries for unlabeled documents with this prompt. Using a filtering mechanism to pick the most suitable document-query pairs, enhancing the training set quality. Benefits of Soft Prompts in DR Incorporating soft prompts into DR brings several advantages: Customization : Tailoring prompts for specific tasks or domains is straightforward. Enhanced Quality : The method produces more relevant queries, which improves retrieval accuracy. Efficiency : Generating training data from existing documents eliminates the need for extensive manual data collection. Testing SPTAR Our experiments, which were conducted with open-source models across various datasets and DR models, demonstrated SPTAR's superiority over traditional methods and other data augmentation techniques. A crucial element of its success was the soft prompt filter, which significantly improved the selection of quality training examples. Findings and Future Directions The data clearly shows that SPTAR significantly boosts DR model performance. The ability of soft prompts to generate relevant queries and the positive impact of the soft prompt filter on data quality were particularly notable. Looking forward, SPTAR's methodology presents exciting possibilities for AI engineers working on search and recommendation systems, offering a scalable way to enhance DR models with quality data. Future research might explore multi-task learning and more sophisticated prompt tuning methods. Conclusion Soft Prompt Tuning for Augmenting Dense Retrieval marks a significant advancement in IR technology. SPTAR provides a viable solution for the common issue of lacking specialized training data, promising to revolutionize efficiency and effectiveness in DR models. As LLMs and prompt tuning evolve, we anticipate even more groundbreaking developments in IR systems. title: Enhancing Patient Experience with On-Demand 3D Printed Aligners
summary: enhancing-patient-experience
body_text: In the world of orthodontic treatment, the patient experience is paramount. As technology advances, so too does the opportunity to provide care that is not only effective but also highly tailored to each patient's needs. Among the most transformative advancements in recent years is the ability to produce 3D printed aligners on-demand, right in the orthodontist's office. This innovation is reshaping expectations and elevating patient satisfaction through unparalleled customization, speed, and engagement. Customization at Its Core The journey to a perfect smile is deeply personal, and with 3D printing technology, orthodontists can offer a level of customization previously unimaginable. Each aligner is designed to fit the unique dental structure of the patient, crafted from precise digital scans of their mouth. This tailor-made approach not only ensures a better fit but also contributes to more efficient and comfortable treatment. Patients can now enjoy the confidence that their treatment is designed specifically for them, addressing their individual needs with the utmost precision. Speed That Speaks Volumes One of the most significant benefits of on-demand 3D printed aligners is the dramatic reduction in waiting times. Traditionally, the process from dental impressions to receiving aligners could take weeks, as molds were sent off-site for manufacturing. Now, with the advent of in-office 3D printing, this timeline is reduced to just a few hours or days. This rapid turnaround not only enhances the overall patient experience by getting them started on their treatment journey sooner but also demonstrates the practice's commitment to leveraging cutting-edge technology for the benefit of its patients. Engagement Through Innovation The process of 3D printing aligners in-office doesn't just streamline production; it also opens the door for greater patient engagement. Orthodontists can involve patients in the treatment process, showing them the technology at work and even providing a glimpse into how their aligners are made. This transparency and inclusion foster a deeper connection between patients and their care providers, enhancing trust and satisfaction. Additionally, the ability to quickly adjust and reprint aligners as needed means that patients feel heard and supported throughout their treatment journey, knowing that their feedback can lead to immediate action and improvement. The Impact on Patient Satisfaction The introduction of on-demand 3D printed aligners into orthodontic practice represents a leap forward in patient-centered care. The customization ensures treatments are as effective as they are comfortable, the speed at which aligners are produced minimizes wait times and maximizes enthusiasm, and the level of engagement with the treatment process strengthens the patient-practitioner relationship. Together, these factors significantly enhance patient satisfaction, setting a new standard in orthodontic care. In conclusion, the evolution of 3D printing technology and its application in producing on-demand aligners directly in the orthodontist's office is more than just a technical achievement; it's a transformation in the way patients experience their journey to a better smile. By prioritizing customization, speed, and engagement, orthodontic practices can offer an unparalleled level of service, making the path to perfect teeth faster, more personal, and more satisfying than ever before. ‍

title: Launching 2 New Developer Tools: LSP and VS Code Extension
summary: Announcing 2 new developer tools for SpiceDB: a Language Server Protocol implementation within SpiceDB and a new extension for Visual Studio Code that provides the capabilities of Playground!
body_text: Announcing 2 new developer tools for SpiceDB: a Language Server Protocol implementation within SpiceDB and a new extension for Visual Studio Code that provides the capabilities of Playground! Earlier this year, we open sourced the SpiceDB Playground , the tool AuthZed built for easy development and testing of SpiceDB Schema . The Playground provides not only syntax highlighting and formatting, but also validation and testing tooling, to streamline development of ReBAC-style authorization systems. Since launching Playground a few years ago, we’ve had a number of users ask for capabilities similar to the Playground, but natively in their own IDEs (integrated development environments) or other development environments. Recognizing that developers often have their own preferred environment, today we are quite happy to announce two new capabilities for developing schema for SpiceDB. Language Server Protocol The first new capability we’re announcing is support for the Language Server Protocol in SpiceDB. The Language Server Protocol is a shared protocol for IDEs and other developer tooling that allows tools to request semantic information about a piece of code. In the case of SpiceDB’s new LSP implementation, the standard language server protocol API can be used to request information about the SpiceDB schema provided. The language server protocol in SpiceDB can be run locally via the lsp command: 1 2 3 4 $ spicedb lsp INF configured logging async=false format=auto log_level=info provider=zerolog INF starting LSP server addr=- INF listening for LSP connections on stdin 1 2 3 4 $ spicedb lsp INF configured logging async=false format=auto log_level=info provider=zerolog INF starting LSP server addr=- INF listening for LSP connections on stdin Visual Studio Code (VSCode) Extension Visual Studio Code is a full-featured open source IDE originally created by Microsoft. One of its most powerful and important features is the ability to extend the functionality of the core IDE by writing and publishing VS Code Extension to the extension marketplace. The SpiceDB VSCode Extension provides most of the features found currently in the SpiceDB Playground, but within VS Code itself. The extension can be installed from the marketplace, the GitHub repository or from within VS Code itself by going to the extension manager ⇧⌘X and searching for “SpiceDB”. Here are some of the features currently available in the VS Code extension: Syntax and Semantic Highlighting for SpiceDB Schema The SpiceDB VSCode extension provides both syntax and semantic highlighting of SpiceDB schemas. The semantic highlighting includes marking the use of relation s and permission s in different colors: Real time validation and diagnostics The VS Code extension provides real time feedback about both errors and warnings that are found in the schema, as it is being edited: Automatic formatting for SpiceDB Schema The VS Code extension provides automatic formatting-on-save: Built-in check watch One of the most important features of the SpiceDB Playground is the ability to watch permissions and see how their computation changes as schema and test relationships are modified. To support this feature in the VS Code extension, the AuthZed team constructed a custom panel to host a copy of SpiceDB within VSCode and provide check watches via actual SpiceDB API calls: In a future blog post, we’ll discuss in technical detail how we built the check watch panel. To use the check watch panel, a file containing relationships yaml named {name}.zed.yaml is placed in the same directory as the {name}.zed schema file being checked. The relationships+schema are then evaluated by SpiceDB and used to display the results of the check permissions calls executed against the schema+relationships. Future With the LSP and extension joining the playground and our CLI tool zed , SpiceDB now has a full set of developer tooling for all major environments! Have a question about SpiceDB, schemas or the new tooling? Don’t hesitate to join our Discord to talk to both AuthZed employees and community experts now! body_text: How much does a domain name cost? Well, that depends on the elements we'll discuss here. Read on for the full story, then start your domain search journey with Instant Domains! We've identified a few key things that contribute to the costs of domain names , including demand and scarcity, resale value, brand protection, and SEO value, among others. Let's dive in. The Basics Registries and Registrars There are two key entities in domain trading and management. Think of the domain name system like a real estate market: Registries: Registries are like the land authorities or city planners who manage entire neighborhoods. They keep a central list of all the properties in their area ( top-level domains ), ensuring each address is unique and follows certain rules. Registrars: Registrars are like real estate agents who help people buy and manage properties. When you want to purchase a property (domain name), you go to a registrar, who then works with the land authority (registry) to secure that property for you. They also offer additional services, like helping you with paperwork and maintenance (DNS management and privacy protection). Marketplaces: Platforms like Sedo, Flippa, and GoDaddy Auctions where you can buy and sell existing domain names. Registries, Registrars, and the top-level domains (TLDs) they manage are key in determining domain pricing. Marketplaces are where you go to complete your transactions. How Much Does A Domain Name Cost The average cost of a domain name is between $10 and $20 per year, but the price can vary depending on several factors: $10 to $20 per year for most non-premium TLDs Hundreds to thousands per year for premium names at premium TLDs Aftermarket names that may cost $10-$20 per year to "lease", but could be thousands to millions to buy You can search all domains for sale using our AI-powered search engine and determine the upfront costs. Demand and Scarcity Domain names that are short, memorable, and easy to spell are in high demand. These domains are scarce because only a finite number of such names are available . For example, single-word domains like "hotels.com" or "shoes.com" are highly sought after because they are easy to remember and directly related to popular industries. The high demand and limited supply drive up the prices of these premium domains. Resale Value Domains with popular keywords or strong commercial appeal can be resold for profit. Investors often buy these domains at a lower price, hold onto them, and sell them when the demand increases. This practice, known as domain flipping, contributes to the high cost of valuable domain names. Domains with a history of high traffic or strong backlinks also tend to have higher resale values, making them more expensive. Brand Protection For businesses, securing a domain name that matches their brand is crucial for protecting their online identity. Companies are willing to pay a premium to obtain domain names closely associated with their brand names to prevent competitors from acquiring them. Owning the exact match domain helps maintain brand consistency and customer trust. Additionally, businesses may also purchase variations of their domain name to prevent cybersquatting, where someone else buys a domain name to sell it at an inflated price later. SEO Value Domains that contain relevant keywords can improve a website's SEO. A domain name with a keyword related to the business's industry can rank higher in search engine results, attracting more organic traffic. This SEO advantage can make keyword-rich domain names more valuable and expensive. Age and History Older domains are more valuable because they have had more time to build authority and trust with search engines. A domain with a long history of stable ownership and usage is often seen as more reputable. If a domain has a positive history and existing backlinks, it can be more attractive to buyers, increasing its price. Geographic Relevance Geographically relevant domains, such as those containing city names or country codes, can be highly valuable. Businesses that operate in specific regions often seek these domains to target local customers effectively. For example, a domain like "NewYorkPlumbing.com" would be highly desirable for plumbing businesses in New York City. Niche Market Appeal Domains that cater to a specific niche can also be expensive. If a domain name is highly relevant to a particular industry or hobby, it can attract a targeted audience. Businesses in niche markets may be willing to pay more for a domain that directly appeals to their customer base. Extension Popularity A domain's extension (e.g., .com, .net, .org) can also impact its value. ".com" domains are generally more expensive because they are the most recognized and trusted by users. However, other extensions can be valuable too, especially if they are highly relevant to the domain name or industry, such as ".tech" for technology-related businesses or ".store" for e-commerce sites. Perceived Brandability The brandability of a domain name refers to how well it can be used as a brand. Names that are unique, easy to pronounce, and memorable are often seen as more brandable. Therefore, these domains can create a strong brand identity and are more desirable and expensive. Market Trends Trends in the market can also affect domain prices. If there is a surge in interest in a particular industry or technology, domains related to that trend can become more valuable. For instance, domains related to cryptocurrencies or NFTs have seen significant price increases due to their rising popularity. Legal Considerations Navigating legal considerations is essential when buying and selling domain names. Domains that come with clean legal standing, meaning they are free from trademarks or legal disputes, are more valuable. Potential buyers will pay a premium for domains that won't pose legal risks or complications. Understanding these legal aspects protects your investments and helps you operate within the bounds of the law. Premium Domain Listings Some registrars list certain domains as premium based on market appeal, automatically pricing them higher. These premium listings are often pre-identified by registrars due to their high demand and potential value, making them more expensive right from the start. Memorability Domains that are easy to remember are more valuable, as they help with word-of-mouth marketing and repeat visits. Memorable domains stick in users' minds, making them more likely to return to the site and recommend it to others. Cultural Significance Domains with cultural or societal relevance may also command higher prices due to their perceived value and connection to popular culture or events. For example, domains related to popular media, trends, or historical events can be highly sought after. TL;DR In summary, domains typically run from about $10 to $20 per year, but the price can be driven up significantly depending on several factors. These include demand and scarcity, resale value, brand protection, SEO value, and domain age, among other factors we discussed. By understanding these diverse factors, beginners can make more informed decisions when purchasing domain names, ensuring they invest wisely and effectively in their online presence.

title: Digital procurement: o que é esse conceito e qual a importância?
summary: Entenda tudo sobre digital procurement, incluindo benefícios, impacto no seu negócio, e como montar e implementar essa estratégia no seu negócio
body_text: Digital procurement é o termo utilizado para elucidar a digitalização amplificada de todas as etapas necessárias para garantir o abastecimento de uma empresa. Em outras palavras, significa utilizar a tecnologia de forma abrangente nos processos de supply chain de um negócio. Parte da transformação digital da cadeia de suprimentos vivida nos mais diversos setores econômicos, o digital procurement traz vantagens como: otimização do fluxo de contratação de aquisições; aprimoramento da gestão de fornecedores; diminuição dos gastos operacionais; aumento da produtividade dos profissionais desse setor, entre outros. A questão é que, por mais que resulte em todos esses benefícios, ainda é comum encontrar gestores que esbarram em alguns obstáculos na hora de digitalizar as etapas de compras de suas empresas. Entre os três mais significativos, os quais foram identificados pela McKinsey & Company , estão: não definir adequadamente o objetivo da digitalização da supply chain; pensar mais no que a nova tecnologia adquirida pode fazer do que no valor que esse recurso pode gerar para a companhia; considerar apenas os desafios que precisam ser resolvidos no setor de procurement, e não na empresa em sua totalidade. Se a sua companhia está passando por dificuldades como essas, ou precisa digitalizar sua cadeia de suprimentos, siga a leitura deste artigo e confira o que é digital procurement, quais retornos positivos traz, como montar uma estratégia para implementação desse conceito e o que esperar do futuro do procurement. O que é digital procurement? Em português, digital procurement significa compras digitais. Com essa tradução já é possível entender que esse conceito consiste na utilização da tecnologia para a realização das tarefas características desse setor. Aqui, é preciso deixar claro que, na supply chain, procurement engloba todas as etapas que garantem o abastecimento de uma empresa. Isso significa que estão inseridas nesse contexto as atividades necessárias para o fluxo ideal de uma cadeia de suprimentos, por exemplo: identificação de demandas; definição de um planejamento de aquisições; bom controle financeiro visando reduzir gastos; identificação dos fornecedores certos; homologação dos terceiros; contratação desses parceiros de negócios; controle de recebimento dos insumos e/ou serviços. Para fazer tudo isso com bons resultados, não basta utilizar um ou outro software que atenda apenas atividades pontuais. O uso de soluções realmente abrangentes, que contam com tecnologias modernas como Inteligência Artificial (IA) e suas ramificações, a exemplo da Machine Learning , é a definição clara do que é digital procurement. Salientando ainda que o uso de um sistema adequado para gerenciamento de toda a cadeia de suprimentos de um negócio faz toda a diferença para o seu sucesso. 5 exemplos de digital procurement São muitos os exemplos que podemos dar de digitalização das atividades de procurement. Então, separamos alguns dos mais interessantes, que são: requisições de compras : digitalizar esse documento interno ajuda a automatizar seu fluxo de criação, envio e recebimento, além de permitir rastreá-lo rapidamente sempre que necessário; gestão de contratos : contratos digitais são preenchidos e ajustados de maneira mais dinâmica, além de garantir um armazenamento mais seguro, e permitir o recolhimento on-line de assinaturas, reduzindo o tempo de finalização do processo; análise de dados : por meio de tecnologias como Inteligência Artificial, a análise de grandes volumes de dados é feita de forma rápida, simples e dinâmica. Os insights gerados podem (e devem) ser usados para embasar decisões e deixá-las mais estratégicas; integração de setores : é essencial que a área de compras mantenha uma boa comunicação com marketing, vendas, financeiro, jurídicos, entre outros departamentos. Sistemas como ERPs promovem essa integração e a troca de informação entre os setores; automação por robôs : por meio do RPA (Robotic Process Automation) é possível eliminar tarefas manuais, como digitação de dados e emissão de relatórios, reduzir erros e aumentar a produtividade dos times. Entenda mais sobre essa tecnologia lendo o artigo: “ RPA: o que é? Saiba como potencializar a tecnologia no processo de compras ” Qual o impacto do digital procurement no setor de compras? **O setor de compras precisa ser tratado como um dos pilares de crescimento estratégico de qualquer negócio. ** Afinal, é a partir do que é adquirido por essa área que todas as atividades da companhia são realizadas. Deste modo, se gerar aumento nos gastos ou perda de qualidade, tudo o que vier em seguida é comprometido. Considerando o nível de responsabilidade e o reflexo que causa no sucesso de uma empresa, é certo dizer que o setor de compras não pode falhar — ou, ao menos, tentar falhar o mínimo possível. Se considerarmos que tarefas feitas manualmente aumentam as chances de erros, além de tomarem boa parte do tempo dos profissionais, fica fácil entender o impacto positivo do conceito digital procurement nesse setor. Por meio da digitalização das atividades de compras é possível: aumentar a eficiência do fluxo de aquisição; mitigar riscos; garantir a conformidade; promover a sustentabilidade; gerar inovação. Tudo isso acontece porque a tecnologia ajuda a levantar dados, analisar documentos, fazer comparações, e muitas outras tarefas com mais rapidez, precisão e segurança. Porém, se mesmo após essa explicação ainda tiver dúvida de por que digitalizar processos de compras, veja no tópico abaixo alguns dos benefícios que podem ser obtidos com essa prática. Quais são as principais vantagens de digital procurement? Para ficar mais claro quanto a digitalização de procurement pode fazer diferença na dinâmica de uma empresa e em seus resultados, listaremos agora as suas principais vantagens, que são: automatização de tarefas repetitivas; redução de custos operacionais; geração de insights por meio da análise de dados; aprimoramento da gestão de fornecedores. Veja detalhes de cada uma a seguir. 1. Automatização de tarefas repetitivas Assim como outros setores, o de procurement também tem uma série de tarefas que são repetitivas e até burocráticas, a exemplo da conferência da documentação apresentada pelos potenciais fornecedores. Realizar manualmente atividades como essas, além de demandar muito tempo, aumenta as chances de erros. Esses, por sua vez, podem impactar, significativamente, o fluxo dos processos e, até mesmo, gerar perdas financeiras importantes. Por outro lado, ao contar com a tecnologia certa, os profissionais de procurement ganham em produtividade e a empresa, no geral, em garantia de etapas de aquisição mais fluidas, dinâmicas e precisas. 2. Redução de custos operacionais Quando se digitaliza um serviço, o número de erros cometidos tendem a diminuir consideravelmente — isso quando não deixam de existir totalmente. Essa redução de falhas contribui para a diminuição de custos operacionais, a exemplo dos que são gerados devido à necessidade de retrabalho. Somado a isso, é preciso considerar que, quando se tem um sistema direcionado para essa área, comparar e identificar qual o fornecedor mais adequado para o seu negócio se torna bem mais fácil. Um dos motivos é que se tem à disposição funcionalidades que ajudam a analisar qual terceiro oferece o melhor preço sem comprometer a qualidade e, com isso, fazer uma boa relação de custo-benefício antes de fechar a parceria. 3. Geração de insights por meio da análise de dados Seguindo essa linha de raciocínio, a digitalização de procurement gera para a empresa uma base de dados sólida, por meio da qual é possível extrair diversos insights para a definição de estratégias mais assertivas. Quanto a isso, não podemos deixar de destacar que uma tomada de decisão baseada em dados traz resultados muito maiores e mais significativos para o negócio, os quais contribuem diretamente para o seu crescimento. 4. Aprimoramento da gestão de fornecedores Nesse trajeto também está incluído o aprimoramento da gestão de fornecedores , processo que vai desde a pesquisa inicial de potenciais parceiros até o encerramento do contrato firmado. O software da Linkana , por exemplo, é uma plataforma SaaS 100% em nuvem que conta com Inteligência Artificial. Com todos os dados centralizados em um único lugar, é possível: realizar a homologação de fornecedores 90% mais rápido; controlar a atualização e vencimento de informações automaticamente e receber alertas de pendências em tempo real. integrar com todos os ERPs e sistemas de compras existentes, entre várias outras funcionalidades Principais elementos da estratégia de digital procurement O passo a passo de como montar essa estratégia, daremos logo adiante. Antes, é preciso apresentar a você quais são os elementos e as principais ferramentas de digital procurement que podem ser utilizados. Por elementos, entenda tudo aquilo que vai além da contração de bons softwares e aplicativos , por exemplo: definição do fluxo de trabalho do setor de compras e procurement ; construção de relacionamentos sólidos e saudáveis com os stakeholders; capacitação adequada dos profissionais desse setor, abrangendo todos os cargos e níveis hierárquicos. No que se refere às ferramentas de digital procurement, considere toda a parte de tecnologia que pode digitalizar processos e atividades, como: CRM ; ERPs; aplicativos de troca de mensagens instantânea, como WhatsApp e Slack; combinação de diferentes sistemas de gestão de fornecedores. Entenda mais sobre essa última possibilidade lendo o artigo “ Linkana + SAP Ariba: por que usar essas duas soluções simultaneamente? ” Como montar estratégias de digital procurement? Agora que as vantagens da digitalização de procurement ficaram claras, é possível que você esteja pensando em como montar uma estratégia com esse foco para implementar na sua empresa, não é mesmo? Entre os passos sugeridos que podem ser seguidos para adotar essa prática, estão: liste todos os processos de aquisição de insumos e contratação de terceiros do seu negócio; a partir dessa listagem, encontre gargalos que precisam ser solucionados; identifique também quais dores podem ser solucionadas com a resolução desses problemas; pense na empresa como um todo, de modo que ao resolver essas questões o negócio inteiro se beneficie; pesquise por softwares voltados para essa área que podem ajudar com esses pontos, e opte por aquele que realmente atenda às necessidades da sua companhia de ponta a ponta, com a Linkana. O que esperar do futuro do procurement? Apesar de parecer um tanto clichê, é bastante válido dizer que **o futuro do procurement será cada vez mais digital. ** Considerando o cenário já existente, a tendência é que as empresas realizem cada vez menos processos de compras manuais, automatizando todas as tarefas relacionadas a essa área. O volume de dados gerados, por sua vez, contribuirá cada dia mais para tomadas de decisões mais precisas, bem embasadas e com foco total no crescimento do negócio. body_text: A domain name is more than just a web address; it's often the first impression your online presence makes. In today's digital landscape, businesses, brands, and individuals vie for attention; the right domain name can be a game-changer. It serves as your virtual storefront, your online identity, and a crucial component of your overall branding strategy. What's In A Domain Name Consider this: when you hear the name of a company or stumble upon a website, what's the first thing that comes to mind? Chances are, it's the domain name. It's the gateway through which users access your content, products, or services. A memorable domain name can enhance brand recall, improve search engine visibility, and establish credibility in the eyes of your audience. Moreover, domain names are finite resources in the vast digital realm. Securing a domain name that resonates with your brand or aligns with your business objectives can be competitive. So, understanding what will work for your brand before buying domain names is crucial. In the following guide, we'll delve into purchasing domain names, from the initial research phase to setting up your domain and beyond. Whether you're a newcomer or a seasoned investor, this step-by-step guide will equip you with the knowledge and tools needed to navigate the world of domain acquisition effectively. Let's dive in! Before You Buy A Website Domain Before delving into the domain purchasing process, clarifying your objectives is important. Are you acquiring a domain name for business, personal use, or investment purposes? The distinction between these goals can significantly influence the domain name you choose. If you're buying a domain name for your business, selecting one that reflects your brand identity and resonates with your target audience is the first priority. A top-level domain (TLD) such as .com, .net, or .org is often preferred for its credibility and professionalism. If you're wondering: what is a top-level domain ? Check out our handy guide! Investing in a TLD can instill trust and enhance your online visibility, making it easier for potential customers to find and engage with your website. On the other hand, if you're acquiring a domain for personal use, such as a blog or portfolio site, the stakes may be different. While a TLD can still offer recognition and search engine optimization (SEO) benefits, opting for a less conventional domain extension, such as .me or .io, may be more cost-effective and align better with your goals. In such cases, prioritizing affordability over premium TLDs can be a great decision, allowing you to allocate resources more efficiently without compromising the overall quality of your online presence. Researching potential domain names: Tools and techniques At Instant Domains, we make buying domain names easy! First, search for all available domains for sale using the power of AI! Instant Domains uses powerful AI to comb through millions of records and show you all the domain names for sale. Clear, compelling domain names are valuable business assets. Other parties often register multiple domain names to sell them. Budgeting: How much should you invest in a name? While domain names can vary widely in price, from a few dollars to thousands or even millions for premium domains , setting a realistic budget ensures that you make prudent investment decisions without overextending your resources. Next, consider the purpose and potential value of the domain names you're interested in. If you're looking to buy domain names for personal use or part of a hobby project, you may prioritize affordability and opt for budget-friendly options. However, if you're purchasing domains for business or investment purposes, you might be willing to allocate a larger budget to secure premium names with greater brand appeal and resale potential. Don't forget to factor in the ongoing costs of domain ownership, such as renewal fees and potential add-on services like domain privacy or SSL certificates. These recurring expenses can vary depending on the registrar and the type of domain you choose, so it's essential to account for them when budgeting for your domain portfolio. Your goal is to make informed decisions that maximize ROI while mitigating unnecessary risk. Choosing a registrar Now that you've selected the perfect domain name for your project, let's register it. Selecting the right registrar determines the quality of service you'll receive, pricing, and additional features you'll have access to. Reputation: Opt for a reputable registrar with a track record of reliability and customer satisfaction. Look for reviews and testimonials from other users to gauge their reputation in the industry. Pricing: Compare the registration fees, renewal rates, and additional charges for services like domain privacy or DNS management. While affordability is important, ensure you're not sacrificing quality for a lower price. Domain Management Tools: Evaluate the registrar's domain management interface and the features it offers. Look for user-friendly tools that streamline registration and provide flexibility in managing your domain settings. Customer Support: Assess the registrar's options, including availability, responsiveness, and support channels. Reliable customer support can be invaluable, especially if you encounter technical issues or need assistance with domain-related matters. We recommend GoDaddy for all the reasons mentioned above. Domain privacy: Do you need it? Consider opting for domain privacy protection to safeguard your personal information from public disclosure in the WHOIS database. Domain privacy services typically replace your contact details with those of the registrar or a privacy service provider, helping to prevent spam, identity theft, and unwanted solicitations. What's Next? Establishing email accounts associated with your domain Once you've successfully searched for domain names, purchased, and registered your domain name or name, it's time to set up domain forwarding so you can use your domain name immediately. Setting up professional email accounts linked to your domain name is important because it enhances your business's credibility and helps maintain a consistent brand identity. Most domain registrars offer email hosting services as part of their packages. To set up, you'll need to access your registrar's control panel, create your desired email addresses, and configure the settings to route emails through your new domain. Using a branded email address like info@yourbusiness.com looks more professional than generic ones, leaving a lasting impression on your clients. Again, it's important to determine if the associated costs of hosting services are worth it for your project. If you're running a business, the answer is definitely yes, but if you're looking to sell the domain name or use it for a personal project, the domain email account may not be necessary. Secure your domain: Tips for preventing unauthorized transfers or hacking Securing your domain name prevents unauthorized transfers or hacking. Ensure your domain registrar offers two-factor authentication (2FA), and always keep your contact information updated to receive timely alerts. Additionally, lock your domain to prevent unauthorized transfers. Regularly update your passwords and use a strong and unique combination for each account. Consider opting for WHOIS privacy protection to keep your personal information private. These steps will help safeguard your domain name and provide peace of mind that your online assets are secure. Setting Up Your Domain: Yes, you need a hosting provider too After you buy a website domain, choosing the right hosting provider is crucial for your website's performance. Start by considering reliability, speed, customer support, and cost factors. Shared hosting is a budget-friendly option for small websites, while VPS or dedicated hosting provides more resources and control for larger sites. Compare providers' uptime guarantees and read reviews to gauge customer satisfaction. Look for features like automatic backups, SSL certificates, and easy scalability. Although it's common for one company to offer both services, it's important to understand that web hosting and domain registration are different. Think of it this way: web hosting is like your house (provided by a hosting provider), whereas a domain name is like your address (managed by a domain registrar). Some companies that offer both are GoDaddy, Squarespace, and Namecheap. Connecting Your Domain to Hosting: DNS Settings and Configuration Connecting your domain name to your hosting provider involves configuring DNS (Domain Name System) settings. Begin by logging into your domain registrar's control panel and locating the DNS management section. Here, you'll need to update the nameservers to those provided by your hosting provider. This process may take up to 48 hours to propagate fully. Once the DNS settings are updated, you can manage your website files and emails through your hosting account. Proper configuration of these settings ensures your domain name points to your website correctly, enabling users to access your site seamlessly. Now that you have your domain name purchased, registered, and hosted! It's time to start building the website itself. Can you build it yourself, or do you need to hire a professional? The answer to that will depend on your personal skills and the bandwidth you have to DIY. DIY website builders like Wix, Squarespace, and WordPress offer user-friendly interfaces and customizable templates, making it easy for beginners to create a website without coding skills. Still, some HTML, CSS, and Adobe Creative Suite knowledge goes a long way here. On the other hand, hiring a professional web developer can provide a more custom and sophisticated design optimized for performance and user experience. Consider your budget, time, and the complexity of your website when deciding which option is best for your business. So You Think You Can Flip? Domain flipping involves buying domain names at a low cost and selling them at a higher price for profit. While it can be lucrative, it's important to understand the risks and rewards. Successful domain flippers invest time researching and identifying valuable domains, often focusing on keywords, brandability, and market trends. Domains, that have already been optimized for search, can attract more traffic and have higher resale value. Brandable domains, which are unique and catchy, appeal to businesses looking for a memorable online identity. Expired domains, previously registered but not renewed, often come with existing traffic and backlinks, adding to their value. By focusing on these types of domains, you increase your chances of making a profitable sale. Knowing where to look is key. Marketplaces like GoDaddy Auctions, Sedo, and Flippa offer extensive listings of domains for sale. Tools like Estibot and GoDaddy Domain Appraisal can help you evaluate a domain's worth. Platforms like ExpiredDomains.net and NameJet are invaluable for finding expired domains. Unlike other investments, domain names may take months or even years to sell profitably. Be patient and keep up with trends! However, not all domains will sell quickly; some may never sell. The key is to be patient and strategic, continuously learning and adapting to market demands. With diligence and savvy, domain flipping can become a profitable venture. We wrote more extensively in our domain flipping guide . If you're purchasing domains for cold outreach campaigns, check out our guide on choosing cold outbound domains . TL:DR Buying a domain name is a fundamental step in establishing your business online. Each step is a building block in creating your online brand identity, from understanding the basics of domain names and selecting a great name to securing your domain and setting up domain email accounts. Then, choosing the right hosting provider and connecting your domain ensures your website runs smoothly, whether you build it yourself or hire a professional. For those interested in domain flipping, understanding the market, selecting valuable domains, and navigating trends are key to success. Patience and networking with other investors can significantly enhance your domain investing journey. You can protect your investments and maximize your online business potential by avoiding common pitfalls such as overpaying for domains and neglecting renewal dates. Whether for business use or hobby, mastering these steps will set you on the path to success in the domain world. title: Lessons From Going Big at Our First Conference
summary: > Having a booth at a major conference can be a game-changer for your startup. Here are some tips from our experience at AICPA Engage 24, where we got a 20" x 30"
body_text: Having a booth at a major conference can be a game-changer for your startup. Here are some tips from our experience at AICPA Engage 24, where we got a 20" x 30" booth, speaking slot, got hundreds of leads, made mistakes and learned a ton. Truewind is AI-powered accounting. We built a digital accountant that does the journal entry work to close the books. Many founders know us for our end-to-end bookkeeping solution. Accounting firms know us for our Month-End Close product. Getting in front of accounting firms is hard - they're not on Bookface, Product Hunt, Hacker News, ... The conference route is a good idea for startups selling to finance and accounting groups. Partners of accounting firms, execs of internal finance teams, CIOs (i.e. decision makers and buyers) go to these conferences to find software vendors. We went to the AICPA Engage conference in Las Vegas. This is the largest accounting conference in the US. 3,500+ accountants spend 3 days in Vegas getting caught up on their CPE credits (continued professional education). Highlights This was our first conference as exhibitors - for Truewind and as individuals We decided to go big : we got a 20" x 30" booth (the second largest space) In addition a speaking slot, 13" tall booth structure, swag, artisan swag, and other neat ideas As a result, we got hundreds of sales qualified leads and closed an enterprise deal within 2 weeks of the conference Overall, it was a success. The feedback from prospects was very positive Things that went well Going big drew attention - I've read posts about cost effective ways to do well at a conference. We decided to go big because we were the new kid on a block filled with familiar faces. Our approach of making a splash worked, and we ended up having roughly 30 people hanging around our booth at any given time. Booth design - It's hard to know exactly how much of our foot traffic was attributed to the booth design, but it definitely made us stand out. The backlit Truewind logo, video wall, and our flashy Las Vegas-themed photo wall drew attention from a distance. Coffee stand - From an ROI perspective, our coffee stand was the best investment. It was relatively cheap compared to other expenses, yet brought in a ton of people. We had a barista pouring steamed milk in the shape of our logo, and bright Truewind stickers on every coffee cup. The level of detail we invested into our branding really paid off, especially since it created visibility far beyond our booth. For example, when attendees went over to a trash bin to throw something away, our cups and logo were everywhere. Also, make sure you get good snacks - avoid bland/generic stuff. Swag strategy - For swag, we categorized our items into high, medium, and low-value tiers. High-value items: Reserved for people who took the time to meet with us for a demo. We opted for premium products like Stanley Cups and high-end battery block chargers. Over-indexing on high-value swag was the right move; it directly contributed to the large number of demos and deeper engagements we got. Medium-value items: These were given out to select individuals who showed genuine interest in our product but might not have had the time for a full demo. Here, we had sunglasses, hats and phone stands. Low-value items: Handed out to anyone who stopped by our booth - these items were meant to create initial engagement/brand awareness, and included tote bags and laptop stickers. Also, everyone got artisan coffee and specialty snacks; technically not swag, but they were definitely our most in-demand medium/low-value items. Building up a crowd - Jia, one of our engineers, gave a demo to a group of five people. Quickly, that small crowd grew to ten, and then fifteen. This happened because when you see a group huddled around something, you want to know what they're up to. Our learning: We have cool things to show! We'll plan a schedule of talks next time on various topics around our booth. Another thing: as a Silver Sponsor, we had 16 tickets but only 10 team members at the event. If you have extra tickets, give them to your customers or partners, invite them to stop by your booth and encourage them to bring other people along as well. Their presence is an easy way to create the impression of a busy and buzzing booth, and attract even more foot traffic. Teamwork - I'm so proud of the execution from my team. A big reason that things ran so smoothly was because of our preparation, communication and clear role assignments. Having that kind of structure in place was especially important when it came to giving demos, which is an area that not everyone is equally familiar with. Beforehand, we'd identified our team members with the most experience and made it clear that they should take the lead on demos. For those with less experience, there was no pressure to present unless they felt ready. Having that delineation of responsibilities ensured that every demo was delivered effectively, maintaining a high standard of engagement with potential leads. With 10 of us there, we had stellar coverage throughout every phase of the conference - especially during peak times. Also, in terms of our mindset, we were optimizing for something that was just as important as operational excellence: having lots of fun. We made a point of turning Engage into a mini offsite and team-building activity. This approach ensured that we had enough hands on-deck, and was a great way for us to bond, collaborate under real-world pressure and overcome challenges together. Following up with leads - Within a week of attending Engage, we published a recap about the conference on our blog. The quick turnaround was intentional; we wanted to leverage the article's publication to reconnect with leads we met at the conference, as well as older leads that we'd been meaning to touch base with. This approach provided a natural and valuable touchpoint, giving us a valid reason to reach out without appearing pushy. Specifically, our event recap served as a perfect conversation starter, allowing us to highlight the impact we made at the conference and keep the dialogue going. You can use data enrichment tools like Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Demandbase, and Apollo to get the contact information you need. We used Persana AI, one of our fellow YC batchmates! Things we could've done better Dealing with conference WiFi - One of our biggest challenges was relying on the convention's WiFi for running technical demos. High-traffic environments can severely strain the WiFi, leading to unreliable connections. We learned the hard way that using mobile data as a backup is crucial for seamless demo experiences. So, ensure you have a robust mobile data plan or portable hotspot to avoid disruptions. Bringing toys for swag - We missed an opportunity by not including toys with our swag. Quan, one of our engineers, suggested that toys would be a big hit, especially for attendees looking to bring something back for their kids or grandkids. Sure enough, this was something that several people mentioned when they stopped by our booth, but we didn't have any to give out. Next time, we're adding toys and more fun/memorable items into our swag lineup. Advertising our speaking slot - Our speaking slot didn't draw the crowd we hoped for. To be fair, it did generate leads, but the engagement level was way lower compared to our booth. Here, the learning is to promote your speaking session more aggressively and do everything possible to align it with high-traffic times. Extra demo prep - Although our overall preparation was solid, we realized that there were specific aspects of our demo presentation strategy that could've been done better. Specifically, we should have spent more time ensuring that every team member, especially those with less demo experience, had more practice, feedback and opportunities to refine their pitches. Some other lessons Know your audience - If you're thinking about having a booth at a conference, the first step is making sure that the right crowd will be there. For accounting, AICPA Engage is a major event with thousands of industry professionals. By talking to past attendees and exhibitors, we knew the perfect audience would be present: senior decision-makers ready to buy. Know the booths around you - We didn't score a spot near the entrance; we were actually two or three rows in. Our team knew that CPA.com would be nearby and that their banner might obstruct the view to our booth. So, we did our homework. After checking CPA.com's historical layout at Engage, we noticed a pattern: they always had a hanging banner, but their structures from the ground up weren't that high. Using that insight, we designed our booth to capitalize on this. We made sure that our Truewind sign was taller than their banner and visible from the moment attendees walked into the exhibit hall. It was a simple tweak, but made a huge difference in drawing attention to our booth. Make sure your product is ready - You'll be giving a lot of demos, and need to feel confident in what you're presenting. If you're on the fence about this, err on the side of caution - there's always another event you can attend later on. Don't overthink your sponsorship level - We were a Silver Sponsor; the Truewind logos around the conference were great to see but that wasn't what we optimized for. We aimed to have a big presence and the booth experience was a bigger driver of that. Conclusion The AICPA Engage conference was our first big GTM investment and it took a lot of meticulous planning from our group to make it happen. My last parting thought for any founder considering whether to invest in a conference booth: Making a splash isn't just about the size of the booth or the money spent; though it helps! Have a deep understanding of who you're targeting and their buying patterns. Make sure the right people are there. Seize every opportunity to stand out (our Las Vegas-themed photowall) and try to attract passersby (our coffee stand). The energy and hustle of your team members does help you stand out. Prospects will respond to that. Ultimately, your booth experience is part of the customer experience. Even though it's not the product per se, it's a representation of the company. Have a good show!

title: To What Extent Is Estimating Effort Beneficial to Squads: Does It Help or Hinder Us?
summary: By James Lawrence
body_text: Press enter or click to view image in full size To What Extent Is Estimating Effort Beneficial to Squads: Does It Help or Hinder Us? Global Engineering 4 min read · Jun 10, 2024 -- By James Lawrence In the world of agile development, estimating effort is a common practice. It involves predicting the amount of work required to complete a task, often quantified using story points. But does this practice actually benefit software teams, or does it create more obstacles than it removes? Key Definitions Before we go any further, it’s important to align on the meaning of the two terms below: Estimating effort helps teams plan the amount of work they can realistically complete within a given timeframe. Story points are numerical values assigned to tasks based on their complexity, often following the Fibonacci sequence (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, etc.). These numbers help teams gauge the relative effort required for different tasks. When I first encountered these concepts, they seemed straightforward. However, I soon realised that estimation practices are highly subjective and can vary significantly between teams. This lead me to explore whether estimating effort is truly beneficial or if it might actually hinder team productivity; comparing the use of Story Points with the popular industry standard approach of #NoEstimates. Using Story Points In my role as a Delivery Manager for the Radio Fulfilment (aka gSchedule) team, I observed that our team lacked a consistent estimation process. The velocity (the number of story points committed vs. completed per sprint) appeared low due to inconsistent ticket sizing (despite a lot of work being done). This made it difficult to report on performance, confidently plan work going into sprints and create timelines. To address this, I implemented a bucket system for estimation, where the team quickly discussed and sized all tickets into swim lanes. This method helped us calculate a more accurate velocity, averaging 56.4 points per sprint compared to the previous 9.4 points. The benefits were clear: Accurate Reporting : Consistent estimation enabled more accurate performance tracking. Credible Planning : With reliable data, we could commit to release dates with greater confidence. Enhanced Coordination : Our improved planning process facilitated better coordination with other teams, especially as we moved towards self-service. The No Estimates Approach Not all teams find value in estimating effort. The #NoEstimates movement, popularized by Woody Zuill, questions the purpose and effectiveness of traditional estimation methods. Here’s why some teams prefer not to estimate: Focus on Value : Shifting focus from estimating tasks to delivering customer value encourages prioritizing features based on their importance rather than complexity. Reduced Overhead : Estimating can be time-consuming and sometimes leads to unproductive disagreements within the team. Improved Collaboration : Less time spent on estimation means more time for collaboration and breaking down work into smaller, manageable tasks. For instance, the gPO team works in Kanban and does not estimate effort. Instead, they track the average weekly number of tickets completed. This then allows them to monitor throughput by comparing the issues created versus resolved against their average. Get Global Engineering’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Remember me for faster sign in Comparing the Two Approaches Both techniques have pros and cons; their effectiveness can also depend on the team’s experience and working style. Story Points Pros : Versatile Planning : Allows teams to adjust their plans based on the specific work at hand. Momentum : Anecdotally, developers who size their own work can feel a greater sense of ownership and drive to meet delivery goals. Cons : Time-Consuming : Estimation can lead to lengthy discussions and disagreements. Inconsistent Reference Points : Without regular reflection, the accuracy of estimates can vary over time. No Estimates Pros : More Time for Development : Developers spend less time on estimation and more on actual development. Agile Focus : Prioritises features based on user value rather than complexity. Cons : Consistency and Experience in Story Splitting Required : Throughput tracking without estimating requires tickets to be of a similar size, so that the calculated average accurately represents the throughput. Stories must be broken down consistently to the same granular level eg. ~3 days or less to complete each Story. Conclusion: Does Estimating Effort with Story Points Help or Hinder? Based on my personal experience, I believe that estimating with Story Points is beneficial. Particularly for newer or changing teams that could benefit from a clear structure and more driven communication. For the Radio Fulfilment example, implementing a consistent estimation process improved visibility over our throughput and planning accuracy. It’s important to note that, estimation practices should evolve with the team — it’s important to keep the technique relevant to current performance and needs. Ultimately, the approach used to estimate effort depends on the team. It is a subjective technique and there isn’t a “correct” way of doing it. Teams should choose the method that best supports their workflow, ensuring they base their planning and reporting on accurate data. Regardless of the approach, tracking progress consistently and with team buy-in is crucial for delivering work with credibility.

title: Why you should invest in self service support
summary: 3 compelling reasons why you should consider jumping on this trend!
body_text: Why you should invest in self service support 3 compelling reasons why you should consider jumping on this trend! Anne-Charlotte Chauvet Anne-Charlotte Chauvet • Published on Jun 3, 2024 • Best Practices Customer Success Table of Contents 1) Customers expect and prefer self service support 2) 24/7 availability 3) It’s cost effective A strategic move for 2024? Do not index In the customer support and success space, one major trend companies are looking at is the shift towards self service support. Self-service support is the use of FAQs, help center, chatbots and other tactics to allow their customers to find answers to their questions autonomously, without having to ask a support representative. Below are 3 compelling reasons why you should consider it! 1) Customers expect and prefer self service support 💡 2 important stats: 88% of customers expect brands to have an online self-service portal . 67% of customers prefer self-service over speaking to a company representative. This customer preference is driven by the convenience, speed, autonomy and control self-service provides. For instance, instead of waiting on hold to speak with a support agent, or waiting on an email reply, customers can quickly find answers through help centers or AI-powered chatbots. This not only enhances their experience but also fosters a sense of independence and satisfaction. 2) 24/7 availability Your customers may be located in various timezones. Either because you’re selling internationally or simply because your users are working remotely. Providing support 24/7 then becomes a necessity. Self service support tools provide round-the-clock availability, ensuring that help is always at hand, regardless of the time of day. Imagine a customer facing an issue late at night. Instead of waiting until business hours for a solution, they can access your self-service portal and find the information they need immediately. This constant availability can significantly enhance customer loyalty and trust. Customers who attempt to self serve, fail, and are forced to pick up the phone are 10% more likely to be disloyal than those customers who were able to fully resolve their issues in their channel of choice. ( HBR ) 3) It’s cost effective Traditional customer support channels, such as call centers and email support, require significant human resources and infrastructure. On the other hand, self service support platforms can handle a large volume of inquiries with minimal human intervention. 81% of all customers attempt to take care of matters themselves before reaching out to a live representative. ( HBR ) Capitalise on customer behavior and provide them with information first hand, so they don’t have to contact you directly. Moreover, by reducing the workload on support agents, you can allocate resources to more complex issues that require personalized attention, and as a result improve overall efficiency and customer satisfaction. A strategic move for 2024? Making enhancements and initiatives to bring your support and customer success self serve is not only a trend but an expectation to drive your customer satisfaction up. You can highly benefit from it by reducing human touch, related costs, and increase customer satisfaction at the same time.
